discrepancies.documentEffect: docs/PUBLIC-VERIFICATION.md's subcommand table row is corrected from `list` to `--list` (old wording kept in the A25 receipt)
discrepancies.queued: make `list` a real subcommand, or remove it from the help and the refusal message; a flag and a subcommand of the same name is a trap
discrepancies.statement: `--help` calls the positional value 'a subcommand name, `all`, or `list`', the unknown-subcommand message lists `list` among the known names, and `main` writes `name = args.command or "list"`; but no dispatch branch accepts `list`, so `verify.py list` and a bare `verify.py` both print "unknown subcommand 'list'" and exit 2. The only accepted form is the `--list` flag, and that is the form the surface declares.
discrepancies.surfaceEffect: command `list` declares `invocation: ["--list"]`; the bare word is never claimed
discrepancies.title: `list` is advertised as a subcommand and is refused as one

witness.observedHead: verify: unknown subcommand 'list'; known: manifest, rebuild, proofs, differential, instruments, controls, receipts, clai
verify: unknown subcommand 'list'; known: manifest, rebuild, proofs, differential, instruments, controls, receipts, clai

discrepancies.documentEffect: a clause naming the exception is added to the descriptive document's `--json` paragraph (old wording kept in the A25 receipt)
discrepancies.queued: either honour `--json` on the discovery commands or reject the combination; a silently ignored flag is not a public argument
discrepancies.statement: `verify.py --list --json` prints the tab-separated listing and exits 0; it does not emit a JSON document, because the listing branch returns before serialisation. The help text describes `--json` as 'emit one machine-readable document' without an exception, and the descriptive document repeated that sentence. The surface declares the observed behaviour: the listing is TSV and only step runs emit a document.
discrepancies.surfaceEffect: `list`/`explain` declare `jsonForm: none`; the discovery block records `emitsJson: false`
discrepancies.title: `--json` is accepted by the discovery commands and ignored

witness.observation: `--list --json` emits tab-separated text, not a JSON object

discrepancies.statement: `--list` takes precedence over `--explain`, which takes precedence over running the named command; `--json`, `--network` and `--tmp` have no effect on `--list` or `--explain`. The behaviour is stable and defensible, but it was in no document, so a caller could not tell which output to expect from `--list --explain`.
discrepancies.surfaceEffect: the precedence is part of the documented contract
discrepancies.title: the argument precedence among the discovery commands is undocumented

witness.observation: `--list --explain` prints the listing, not the explanation blocks

discrepancies.documentEffect: the descriptive document's claim that a declared private path is reported present or absent is left unedited: the defect is the tool's, not the prose's
discrepancies.queued: add `artifacts/phase2/install` to the audited root set, or stop declaring it private; then re-derive the presence fields
discrepancies.statement: The three consumer commands declare `artifacts/phase2/install` as a private path, but the interface's audited root set names `artifacts/phase2/shell` instead. The declared path is therefore never counted, so `private_state_present` can never report it and the document's `known_roots` block omits it. A declared private read that presence-reporting cannot see is an under-report, not a declaration.
discrepancies.surfaceEffect: the declaration is transcribed exactly; the surface does not hide the interface's own declaration
discrepancies.title: a declared private root is outside the audited root set

discrepancies.documentEffect: one clause is added to the descriptive document's determinism paragraph (old wording kept in the A25 receipt)
discrepancies.queued: declare the private-state readings as an environment input, or project them out of the compared record
discrepancies.statement: The `environment` block is declared as an input and excluded from the two-run comparison, but `private_state` is a separate top-level block computed from `git status` and is inside the compared record. Two runs over the same checkout therefore differ if an untracked or ignored entry appears between them, and the published sentence excluded only the `environment` block.
discrepancies.surfaceEffect: the determinism rule is declared with its exact scope and this gap named
discrepancies.title: live private-state readings sit inside the deterministic record

witness.observation: the document carries `private_state` at top level, outside the declared `environment` input block

discrepancies.statement: docs/PUBLIC-VERIFICATION.md said `test_verify.py` holds 19 tests in two places. The module currently executes 37. The figure is a live quantity in a descriptive document that no generator corrects, which is exactly the drift the document was written to warn about.

contract.0: every selected required step is PASS; a single requested step gates on itself and must be PASS
contract.1: at least one selected step is not PASS: FAIL, BLOCKED or NOT_RUN. NOT_RUN is never a pass
contract.2: the invocation was refused before any step ran: an unknown subcommand, a malformed argument list, or a surface that cannot be read

notes: The listing, the help text and the explain blocks are the executable's own words; nothing here is copied from the declaration.
The JSON field set is read from one probe run; value-level determinism is the separate two-run comparison in the verdict.
